parallel.requirements: Rebuild Flask-RESTful 0.3.10 behavior under the provided Python/Flask/Werkzeug environment, including core package, tests, docs, examples, config, and release helper obligations.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: Parent kept implementation ownership while also launching a five-task workflow with verifier agents for yield tests, API surface, remaining failures, compatibility, and examples/packaging.
parallel.implementation: Copied upstream 0.3.10 into the workspace, installed editable, repaired reqparse JSON source behavior for Werkzeug 2.1+, added docs theme files, config files, release helper, and example support.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Parent integrated changes into the shared workspace and artifact validation captured a complete workspace tree including package, docs, tests, examples, and generated caches.
parallel.verification: Ran pytest repeatedly, manually drove skipped yield tests, inspected workflow reports and child audits, and observed official evaluation complete with 361 of 362 tests passed.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The workflow never returned an aggregate result before timeout; final.txt is empty, and official evaluation still failed one of 362 cases.

serial.requirements: Rebuild the same Flask-RESTful task from the identical prompt and target hidden-test surface without delegation.
serial.plan_and_ownership: Single parent performed all exploration, copying, patching, docs/examples/config work, release-helper creation, and verification with workflow tools disabled.
serial.implementation: Downloaded/copied upstream Flask-RESTful 0.3.10, applied a similar reqparse request JSON compatibility fix, added docs theme/support files, top-level config, scripts/release.py, and example handling.
serial.integration_and_delivery: All changes were made directly in the serial workspace; artifact validation captured the expected package, docs, examples, config, and support files.
serial.verification: Ran pytest and local probes for examples, API surface, crypto, and legacy yield tests within the parent trajectory before timeout and official evaluation.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial run also timed out with empty final text and the current official evaluation failed one of 362 cases.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the Flask-RESTful 0.3.10 reconstruction task, hidden-test risk, required docs/examples/config/release files, and modern Flask/Werkzeug compatibility obligations.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same prompt and rebuilt the same upstream package, docs, examples, config, tests, and release-helper surface.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No material requirement-recognition difference explains the official result; both ended with the same 361/362 failed outcome.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work into parent-owned local implementation plus a five-task workflow and verifier pipeline, while tracking local TaskCreate items.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial used one parent trajectory with workflows disabled and no subagents or workflow tasks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The decomposition differs sharply: parallel created broad concurrent audit ownership, while serial kept all implementation and verification ownership in the parent.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The workflow prompt gave children shared context about environment, current failures, hidden tests, and read-only verification constraints; no missing brief or cross-agent interface contract failure is directly shown.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial maintained context locally in one trajectory, carrying the same upstream/test/environment facts into each edit and verification step.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more transfer boundaries, but the evidence does not show a task fact lost, stale, conflicting, or omitted in a way that changed implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel copied Flask-RESTful 0.3.10, fixed the reqparse request.json compatibility path, added docs theme/support files, config, examples support, and release helper material.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial copied the same upstream release and made a similar reqparse compatibility fix plus docs/theme/release/config support.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implemented behavior was materially similar; any remaining official miss appears common to both rather than uniquely caused by the parallel code path.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Some child reports returned and were inspected, but the aggregate workflow state ended result null and killed after repeated stall retries.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle; all findings stayed in the parent trajectory and no verifier return was required.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel incurred a workflow result lifecycle that serial avoided; however, the missing aggregate return is downstream of the retained fan-out budget episode, not a separate independent label.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children and parent shared /workspace; one child observed docs/_themes appearing mid-audit and simplexml was installed, but no harmful overwrite or final contamination is proven.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made all workspace and environment changes in one parent context, with no concurrent workspace agents.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel exposed shared-state risk, but the observable consequence did not rise to a retained write or artifact-leakage pattern.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran pytest, manual yield-test checks, child audits, and partial verifier reports, but timed out with no final text and no completed workflow aggregate.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran pytest, examples/API/crypto/yield checks locally and also timed out with no final text.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had more redundant verifier work but not a better final official outcome; both solutions were evaluated and both failed one of 362 tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spent 902,290 workflow child tokens, showed repeated workflow stall retries, returned code 143 at about 2400 seconds, and ended with workflow result null.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial also timed out near 2400 seconds, but with zero workflow child tokens, zero workflow tasks, and no delegation lifecycle.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The task-solving difference is process efficiency and closure: parallel lost budget to a broad killed workflow, while serial used the whole window directly; the official outcome remained the same.

outcome_analysis.explanation: This pair is not discordant under the current completed official evaluations: both parallel and serial scored 361 of 362 and solution_passed false. The concrete difference is process-level: parallel spent substantial workflow child budget on a broad audit/verifier fan-out that was killed without an aggregate result, while serial kept the work in one parent trajectory. That adverse parallel episode did not produce an official outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Broad workflow fan-out and retries consumed child-token and wall-clock budget and ended with result null before timeout.
serial_contributors: Serial avoided delegation and child-result lifecycle overhead while implementing a similar package reconstruction and reqparse fix.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both final artifacts still missed one official testcase, so the remaining failure is common outcome evidence rather than a proven parallel-only coding defect.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is adverse parallel process evidence only

Rejected because the parent owned setup, implementation, verification, and delivery despite timeout; the adverse episode is budget exhaustion, not absence of a pipeline owner.
Rejected because productive implementation began before and during investigation; no mandatory serial preflight blocked all useful work.
Rejected because the parent implemented and created files while child investigations ran; investigation was not a completed serial first phase gating later work.
Rejected as less specific than the broad workflow fan-out and retry budget episode; no separate critical path was starved by auxiliary allocation.

The parallel parent launched one broad workflow with five investigation tasks and a verifier phase; the workflow state shows repeated stall retries, null aggregate result, killed status, and 902,290 workflow child tokens. This is direct collective breadth/retry budget exhaustion that consumed the finite run window and left the parent without the planned aggregate verifier handoff before timeout. The serial control used no workflow or child token budget and still reached the same official score through a single-parent path.
candidates.realized_consequence: The broad workflow consumed 902,290 child tokens, repeatedly retried stalled children, and was killed with result null before the parent timeout, leaving planned verifier aggregation unavailable at closure.
candidates.near_match_reason: Missing Verifier Return is the nearest surface symptom, but no independent concrete verifier finding was trapped; the absent aggregate return was downstream of the killed fan-out/retry budget episode.
